subject: Re: Order form consolidation — SOW exhibit + unit pricing alignment
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@luminexa.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@luminexa.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Consolidate SOW line items + updated PO

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the team's excited to move forward. Procurement asked us to simplify the order form: they want the two separate line items currently in Exhibit B ("Inference Capacity - Std" and "Inference Capacity - Burst") merged into a single consolidated capacity line with an internal breakdown instead of separate SKUs. The goal is to reduce PO complexity and simplify invoicing.

Attached is the PO (Luminexa_PO_98765.pdf). They also asked whether we can reflect a blended unit price for the consolidated line and prorate for the remainder of the term (remaining months on their current term: 8 months).

Could you share a short change order (or redline of Exhibit B) that: 1) consolidates the two line items, 2) shows the blended price and the prorated calculations, and 3) clarifies billing cadence? Procurement would like to review this week.

Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Director, Procurement
Luminexa, Inc.

Subject: Re: Request: Consolidate SOW line items + updated PO

Thanks Sofia — got the PO and the ask. Looping in Rishi (AE) for commercial acceptance and Priyom (Sales Ops / legal coordination) to draft the change order and the redline. Naomi, can you confirm whether we should treat this as a mid-term amendment with prorated charges or apply a true-up on the next invoice cycle?

Proposed plan: 
- Priyom to produce a redline of Exhibit B (sow-exhibit-B-redline.pdf) and a short change order doc that captures the blended unit price and prorate math.
- Rishi to confirm commercial approval on blended price and any required credits for overlapping capacity.
- Naomi to confirm invoicing treatment and impact to revenue recognition.

If we can get a draft by EOD tomorrow I'll share back with Sofia and procurement for a quick review. Priyom — attaching a template I usually use for these (proposed-change-order-draft.docx) and a quick workbook that shows a sample blended price calc (pricing-rebalance-sheet.xlsx).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Customer Success & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-change-order-draft.docx (editable draft), pricing-rebalance-sheet.xlsx (workbook)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Consolidate SOW line items + updated PO

Laura / team — thanks, I reviewed the PO and your template. Quick summary of legal/ops items I recommend we include in the change order (high level):

1) Single consolidated line: replace Exhibit B lines 1 & 2 with one line named "Committed Inference Capacity (consolidated)" with a short internal breakdown table in the SOW appendix (not on the order form) that shows Std vs. Burst allocation percentages.

2) Blended price: capture the blended unit price and include a one-row worked example showing the prorated amount for the remaining 8 months. We'll include the exact formula so procurement can reconcile numbers to their PO.

3) Billing cadence: we should offer two options to expedite approval — (A) prorate remaining months and bill on next invoice, or (B) apply a one-time credit on the next invoice to align historical overpayments. Naomi, option (A) is cleaner for revenue recognition but option (B) is sometimes required by procurement; which do you prefer?

4) Effective date & term: change order effective upon signature, term end remains unchanged, with a note that any future capacity reallocation requires 30 days' notice.

5) Signatures: include DocuSign routing and reference to original MSA and Order Form (MSA v2.1, Order Form #LDX-98765).

I'll redline Exhibit B and populate the template with the blended math. Expect the draft in ~3 hours.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Contracts Specialist, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachment: sow-exhibit-B-redline.pdf (redline), pricing-rebalance-sheet.xlsx (updated)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@luminexa.com>
Cc: procurement@luminexa.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Consolidate SOW line items + updated PO

Hi Sofia — thanks for the PO and patience. We drafted a concise change order and redlined Exhibit B to reflect the consolidated capacity line and the blended unit price; both are attached. Key points: 

• Blended unit price: $0.0235 per token-hour (worked example included).
• Prorate: we applied option (A) — prorate for the remaining 8 months and bill on the next invoice. If procurement needs the alternative (one-time credit), we can swap to option (B) but will need an explicit request.
• Billing: standard monthly invoicing with the prorated amount included on the next invoice; language added to clarify billing treatment.
• Effective date: upon signature.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached change_order_final.docx and sow-exhibit-B-redline.pdf.
2) If acceptable, sign via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/abc123-luminexa-change-order.
3) If procurement prefers the credit approach, reply with "credit-request" and we'll route to finance for approval.

Sofia — quick question for your procurement team: do you need us to put the consolidated line on the PO as a new single SKU, or will you accept a referenced consolidation (we'll keep internal breakdown in the SOW appendix)? Procurement's preference will determine whether we issue a new PO amendment or accept the existing PO with an attached change order.

Happy to hop on a 15-minute call if easier.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Customer Success & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: change_order_final.docx, sow-exhibit-B-redline.pdf
